postTitle: More Than Two Partners: Protecting Everyone
topic: Most money forms were written for two people, and many of them can hold more

assumptions.notes: No figures. From the post: most pension, insurance and investment beneficiary forms allow several names with a percentage each; hospital visitation forms can usually list several people; healthcare and financial powers of attorney name one person at a time with alternates in order; some schemes pay the ongoing survivor pension only to a legal spouse even where a lump sum can go to anyone named. Three common ways to cover that gap: life insurance, savings in the partner's own name, the lump sum.

Can a pension form name three partners? Often, yes. The survivor pension is usually another story.

beats.narration: Many forms take several names. Beneficiary forms on pensions, insurance and investments. Hospital visit forms. And wills, naming each partner in full.
There, households often name everyone, with the share intended. A spouse's legal rights or forced heirship may still limit a will.

beats.narration: Other documents name one person at a time. A healthcare proxy. A financial power of attorney.
Households often name each other as alternates in an agreed order, and agree that whoever is named consults the others.
One form often looks open. A pension lump sum may go to anyone named, the ongoing survivor pension often only to a spouse.

For every form, check whether it accepts several names, what order applies if it does not, and whom any survivor pension covers.

caption.instagram:
Three partners, one pension form. Many forms can name all three, with a share for each.

Beneficiary forms on pensions, insurance and investments often take several names, with a percentage for each. Hospital visit forms can usually list several people. A healthcare proxy or a financial power of attorney names one person at a time, so households often agree an order of alternates. And one form looks open and often is not: the ongoing survivor pension, which many schemes pay to a legal spouse only. Households commonly cover that gap with life insurance, savings in the other partner's own name, or the lump sum where a scheme allows it.

Three checks for every form: can it hold several names, if not what is the order, and what does the pension pay a survivor, and to whom?
